doc_friction.issue: Chaining several '( ... ) &' jobs inside one run_in_background command silently dropped one of them (the permits pull); one background command per long job is safer, worth a line next to the wait_for.py advice.

Two runs drew build-data within a minute and both took the same 'Next' item; the claim-check step only sees pushed PRs. Pushing the pre-registration took ~20 min (after the data pull), by which time the sibling had already pushed theirs; pushing an empty claim commit first, before the pull, would have exposed the collision.

notes: Pre-registered R0-R5 (commit 74d901bd4) before any model run. 32 fits (2 held cities x 4 test years x 4 rules, 3 seeds, q0.9) on a fresh pull with row counts identical to sessions 95-99. SF, the Y-6 selector picks nc3 in all 4 (regret 2.15). Consolidated with sibling session 100 (#16810) as session 101; 2019/2020 fits match theirs to the digit. certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
